utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kupresanin, when we talked, did we notice that there are any dates that are wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First let us take a look at paragraph 1 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Kupresanin, your party, the party that you founded, when did it join the SDS? The 12th of July of which year?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the B/C/S version is correct, and it should be corrected in English version that it's 1990 instead of 1992. Now can we have paragraph 5 on the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To which paragraph does the correction refer, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The previous one or the next one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 1, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph, while reading the statement of Mr. Kupresanin, we found out that in paragraph 5, "page" in this -- from this document was wrongly recorded, and it's not page 52 to 53 but page 57. It was recorded page 35 and should read page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lots of technical matters, Mr. Kupresanin, but you do remember that we corrected some numbers, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 1 now of the statement on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kupresanin, on this page do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Then it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed -- yes, it's not a major thing, but accuracy is always appreciated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Vojo Kupresanin became engaged in political work on the eve of the first multi-party elections. On March the 4th, 1990, he formed the Yugoslav Democratic Party, the Homeland Front, and on the 12th of July, 1990, his party became part of the SDS. After this, he was a deputy in the chamber of citizens in B&H Parliament and a member of the SDS Main Board. In the first half of 1992, Mr. Kupresanin was elected president of the Assembly of the community of municipalities of Bosanska Krajina and in the second half of the same year, president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, ARK. After the war, he reactivated the work of the Homeland Front, and on June the 1st, 2013, he retired. This Union of Municipalities of Bosanska Krajina with acronym ZOBK was established primarily for economic reasons and included 17 municipalities. After World War II, Banja Luka was economically the second most powerful town after Sarajevo and the region had several hundred million dollars of commercial surplus, but all this money went to the central bank of Sarajevo. The ZOBK Assembly adopted its own statute and there were members of the different parties and everybody worked for the same idea, keeping for the people of Krajina the natural resources of the area. The basic goal was being able to follow events in the sphere of the economy, politics, and culture. On June 28th, 1991, the ZOBK Assembly adopted a declaration for the unification of the two Krajinas: RSK and Bosnian Krajina. The ZOBK Assembly had Muslims and Croats who were delegated by municipalities in which they were deputies for the SDA and HDZ until such a time that they stopped coming to the sessions at the instruction of the SDA and HDZ central offices from Sarajevo. Vojislav Kupresanin, in his capacity of president of the ZOBK Assembly, expressed his wish for the ZOBK to be joined by various Muslim and Croat municipalities because ZOBK goal was not to create a Serbian community. Mr. Kupresanin personally contacted Mr. Fikret Abdic, the director of Agrokomerc and a prominent Muslim leader of European orientation because he wanted this food -- his food company to be supplied with the raw material from the area. Unfortunately, Mr. Abdic never replied to these calls. In September 1991, the statute of the ARK was adopted. In this statute, all nationalities were recognised as equal and municipalities with a majority of non-Serbian people were enabled to join the ARK. In order to protect the Serbian people in Slavonia, in Croatia, who were exposed to the most heinous crimes, the Serbs in Krajina turned to the JNA for protection. After JNA General Uzelac refused to intervene to defend the Serbs, the ARK decided to declare a mobilisation. Later on, ARK Crisis Staff was established, even though the Republika Srpska government ordered the formation of the Crisis Staff per municipalities not per regions. The reason for the formation of the ARK Crisis Staff was the tense and alarming situation in B&H. Dr. Karadzic charged Mr. Kupresanin with the responsibility of influencing the leadership in Prijedor to close down investigation centres. Mr. Kupresanin asked those authorities to shut down and to improve the prisoners' living conditions until its disbandment. After that, Mr. Kupresanin toured to Manjaca prisoner of war camp in order to check living conditions there. Furthermore, Mr. Kupresanin negotiated an end to the fighting in Kotor Varos, in agreement with the commander of the VRS operational group and with the chief of the security service centre in Banja Luka. And that was the end of the statement summary of Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any further questions, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, I would kindly ask to have 1D2036 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, could you assist us, that takes us to what paragraph of the statement, if any? I found it already; it's paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, what we have before us is a transcript of an audio recording. You saw this during the proofing. We cannot see what it is on the basis of these first two pages, so could we please have the third page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In B/C/S, we need line 6 onwards and in English line 8 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Sveto Kovacevic is?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I think he was president of the municipality or president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Celinac at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sveto Kovacevic here addresses the deputies, and he says: "I have the honour of opening the constitutional session of the community of Bosanska Krajina municipalities." Did you participate in this session? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is stated in line 15 in B/C/S and line 18 of the English version that Mr. Sveto Kovacevic informed everybody that the representatives of the HDZ, the SDA, and the SDS were all present at this session as delegates. Do you remember whether there were representatives of Muslims and Croats at that session?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: After my election, I addressed them, I greeted them, and I congratulated them on the fact that the community of Bosanska Krajina municipalities had been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now on the same page from line 26 onward, and in English it is in line 31 and line 32, it says that one of the tasks of the session is to elect the president of the municipality. Was the president of the community of Bosanska Krajina municipalities elected?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was elected?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we go to page 4 in both versions, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- before we continue, neither in the statement nor on page 3 where you took us nor anywhere else I find a time-frame when was this meeting held. Could we -- could the witness tell us when and what date this meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 24th of April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this page, we see that Dr. Dusko Jaksic addressed the gathering. He was introduced as the director of the economic institute. Did you know Mr. Jaksic?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, he was the president of that institute as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In lines 22 through 26 in B/C/S and in English from line 30 onwards, and that bit spills over to the following page, Mr. Jaksic says here that he doesn't belong to any of the ruling parties. What was Mr. Jaksic's role? Why was he there? Why was he brought to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: He was perceived as the biggest expert in economy. He had a Ph.D. in economics, he was a scientist. His presentation was not only his presentation, it reflected the way a number of experts were thinking and that's what he presented at that Assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His speech was rather long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 11 in B/C/S and 12 in English. We're interested in line 29 in English and line 26 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is recorded here that the first speaker, Mr. Jaksic, said Banja Luka must not replace Sarajevo. Further on, he continues in line 31 in B/C/S and on page 13 of the English, starting with line 12 onwards, starting with the very end of line 12, we read: "I'd like to see Krajina as a good region and that it becomes the route of a good and stable Bosnia and Herzegovina," obviously in Yugoslavia. Do you agree that that was the objective behind the establishment of that region?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Throughout the entire transcript, there is a lot to be shown; for example, page 15 in B/C/S that I would like to show first and the same bit can be found on page 16 in English. We're interested in line 15 in B/C/S and line 31 in English. It says here: "So it is obvious that there is a strong economic reason for us a regionalise, to link-up, to join certain functions, to unite at the region level" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, from both my colleagues, I received a short question: What's the relevance of this? And it won't be the first one --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We want to show what was the purpose actually of establishment -- establishment of this region, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The region or the economic co-operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The region?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there may have been economic reasons. Is that contested by the Prosecution, that economic reasons may have played a role, perhaps not the exclusive role, but -- and that in 1991, various parties were willing to co-operate?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We don't dispute that at the outset economic motives were one component of the decision to establish such regions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is reflected in this meeting, that component, at least from what we've seen until now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree what people are saying is reflected on the transcript, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- and that they're describing what we've just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will then shortly finish with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can only have page 20 in B/C/S and page 22 in English version. [Interpretation] Line 7 in B/C/S and line 4 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The speaker is recorded as saying: "If we don't care who lives in these areas, if we disregard who's Serb, who's Croat, who's Muslim, we'll hopefully still remain living together. But it's important that wherever anybody lives, be it a Serb, a Croat, a Muslim, that this person lives well, that's our main goal." Do you remember that that was precisely the intention? Was there a hidden agenda? What was the intention behind the establishment of the region?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: You lived in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the state which was called Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It had its laws, it had its constitution. We observed that constitution and, according to Article 4 of that constitution, we were allowed to make associations for economic reasons, and I mean several municipalities could unite in order to control taxes, health care, the education system, and other things like that. The main reason and the main idea was to improve the economic situation and to improve the life of the people who lived there. We wanted to spend fewer hours in Sarajevo and more time in the region where the resources were and where the income was generated. That was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you started your answer by saying: "You lived in Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." Who is "you" in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant I lived --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when I said "you," I meant all of us, we.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We would tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of the document? Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we can sit afterwards, Mr. Traldi and me, and try to cut down this -- whatever is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to do that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: SO just then to MFI the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be MFI'd. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D2036 receives MFI number D853, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D853 is marked for identification. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation with paragraph 14 of the statement of Mr. Kupresanin, the Prosecution asked me to lead the evidence on the document marked as 21323. So I would like to have this document on our screens, please; 65 ter 21323.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were seeking the underlying document to be shown rather than the statement, paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, underlying the document. Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have 65 ter 21323 on our screens. And then for English, the English version, please. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kupresanin, this is an intercepted conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're interested in page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This conversation took place between Radovan Karadzic and probably Nenad Stevandic on the 31st of August, 1991. I would like to look at page 3 in B/C/S and 4 in English. There is a reference to the Krajina referendum prior to that. First of all, let me ask you, did Mr. Karadzic oppose the unification of the two Krajinas, the one in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the one in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: The idea for the Krajinas to be united in Croatia and Bosnia was the desire of the Serbs on the both banks of the Una River for a long time. Radovan Karadzic was against that and he fought for Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole. He disputed the idea of a referendum that would pose that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this page in B/C/S, line 8, and in English, line 7, it is recorded that Radovan Karadzic said: "What we want is to keep Bosnia peaceful and out of it -- we have reasons for staying out of it." And now on the following page in English, which is page 5, Mr. Karadzic's inter -- collocutor on line 8, which is line 30 in B/C/S on the same page, he says: "... if Alija announces a referendum in Bosnia-Herzegovina, we would react and announce our own referendum in Krajina." Mr. Karadzic is recorded as saying: "There is no need," and then he swears. And then he says, "God damn, they never listen." And then that same person says: "I'm not involved in all that, Brdjanin is handling that." And so on and so forth. The conversation continues along the same lines. Was Mr. Karadzic always against the unification of those two Krajinas?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic ran in the elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and when he did that he showed that he wanted Bosnia-Herzegovina to be a state where Serbs would be able to exercise their basic rights, to be protected, where the Serbs would be able to develop and advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 21323 receives Exhibit Number D854, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D854 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And one more document, Your Honours. I will be finished with the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another document is in connection with paragraph 41 of Mr. Kupresanin's statement, and I would kindly ask to have 65 ter number on our screens, 16598. [Interpretation] This has to do with financing the army; that that's paragraph of the statement. Also, there's a reference to logistics; logistical support to the Army of Republika Srpska, that is. While commenting on this document in his statement, Mr. Kupresanin pointed out that he had never seen that document, or rather, that he doesn't remember it. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He can tell us what you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, he said what it was that he knew so now I'm going to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the document before you, Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I have trouble reading it, so let me try with my glasses now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 23rd of June, 1992 is the date. It was sent by the 1st Krajina Corps to the Assembly and the government of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I understand. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, it says: "As the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, we are compelled to address you and inform you that we have received a document from the Government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, saying that they will continue funding the Army of the Serbian Republic of BH only until the 20th of May, 1992 ..." The entire document goes along these lines. This is what I'm going to ask you: Do you remember this problem? Do you remember how it was resolved?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, it didn't appear only in Banja Luka, that problem. It was in all the municipalities. Quite simply, the Yugoslav army was withdrawing to Yugoslavia from the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And then we were compelled to make our own army, the Army of Republika Srpska, and to support it. Since Republika Srpska had not been created as a state yet, then it was the municipal budgets that had to support the army. So this was only to be expected, this document, and it circulated through all the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 16598 receives Exhibit Number D855, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do not have any more questions for Mr. Kupresanin. Only if you want me to deal with the associated exhibits, we will not propose three of the documents from the original list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but still a large number remaining, a relatively large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah -- that's that type of the statement, Your Honour. That statement would not be understood properly without the documents since this gentleman commented on the overall situation through the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll consider that. But before we even move to that, I would have a short question in relation to the paragraph that we just looked at, that is paragraph 41, and your answers in relation to the -- to what the document you were not familiar with are about. Witness, in paragraph 41, I read: "Given that the central state was not functioning, someone had to provide logistical support so the burden fell on the municipalities ..." The "central state," was that a reference to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Or was it a reference to the newly established -- what then became the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the newly established Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although what was read from the document at this moment was about the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia not giving any further support. Could I then ask you whether - and then I'm focusing primarily on the paragraph you were asked about - was any support received in whatever way by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia which would support the operations and the functioning of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 20th of May, the Yugoslav army withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina; however, the state of Yugoslavia also withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina. What remained of the Army of Yugoslavia in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina became ours; the technical assets, the equipment that remained. We took that - it belonged to us then - and we attached that to the Army of Republika Srpska. I know that from Yugoslavia we most often received aid in terms of food, medicine, clothing, and these hospitals in Serbia treated our patients if we could not manage that in Republika Srpska. So they helped in different ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you say "food, medicine, clothing," are you meaning -- or are you including food for the army, medicine for soldiers, and clothing for members of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we had to do that too, Republika Srpska, except that Yugoslavia paid for a number of officers. All the rest became the burden of Republika Srpska. Some of the officers who were in the army, and the higher officers withdrew to Yugoslavia and towns in Yugoslavia quite -- actually, very few remained in our parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to go to the line where you say that the central state was not functioning. Does that mean that the newly established republic in no way provided any money and, for example, ammunition, or was it just that you were entirely left to the local communities to provide you with whatever was needed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at first, yes, that way. As for arms, ammunition, we had that; however, as far as food is concerned and some other things that have to do with the army, clothing, then that was done by the local organs of government in the municipality. Until the Republika Srpska was properly established, then some of these resources arrived through the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the time-frame from paragraph 41 is rather limited, that is, in the very early stages of the existence of the newly established republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. Mr. Lukic, perhaps we later deal with the associated exhibits. Let's see what happens during cross-examination and then, at the end, we'll deal with those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Lukic could put the numbers of the three documents he's not going to tender here on the record so that we have a clear picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are not going to tender 09690, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hold on, one second, please. 09 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm trying to find it on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fifth document from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm apparently looking at a different document. Just -- if you just mention them. And then perhaps we already could ask the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Mr. Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next one is 65 ter number 17221; and the third one is 65 ter number 20099.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. We'll take a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't finish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I want to inform Your Honours, that our next witness will be Mr. Lalovic after Mr. Kupresanin when he finishes; it will be on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And let me just have a look. There was some confusion about another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will just push him in front of the two witnesses from Prijedor area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it will not be Mr. -- the other witness -- I didn't mention his name because there was some confusion about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He does not seek protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He does not seek. And I think they were rescinded in the Karadzic case, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the Stakic case, I think. He testified in Stakic case as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He testified in Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So, therefore, there are no protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And one more thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On our scheduling. We provided one witness for the 14th or 15th of January, so it's the one witness we could provide in that week where the Orthodox new year is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And have you informed Chamber staff who it would be and a time, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was just informed about this so we will inform --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we expect you to provide full information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just one clarification, when you were reading the witness summary of Mr. Kupresanin, on page 8, line 21, you said - and it is accordingly recorded - Vojislav Kupresanin. Could you please clarify which is his right first name, Vojo or Vojislav?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously I made a mistake. Your Honour, it's Vojo on his statement, and Mr. Kupresanin, when he introduced himself, said "Vojo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, if you're ready to cross-examine the witness, I'll introduce you to him. Mr. Kupresanin, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find him to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified in the Karadzic case just over a year ago. Is it your position that you told the truth in that testimony?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's also your position that you told the truth in that interview; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, it was so long ago. There's a lot of it that I don't remember, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was a long time ago and much closer to the events described in your statement. Would it be fair to say that your recollection of those events was clearer in 2001 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm going to start with the last topic you discussed with Mr. Lukic, the provision of logistical support to VRS units in the ARK. Now, this Chamber received evidence just two days ago that the 1st Krajina Corps continued receiving logistical support, both weaponry and financial, from the SFRY through the Main Staff. Now, you weren't part of that chain of support yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time I hear of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so you're not aware of the magnitude or extent of the support that the VRS or the 1st Krajina Corps was receiving; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: No. I know that the Yugoslav army, with its generals, and Blagoje Adzic was one of the key generals, they came to us to take the weapons that were located in our parts. They asked for aircraft, tanks, rockets. That's what they were looking for. And they didn't bring in anything. I don't know them bringing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You weren't a member of the VRS in May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: May 1992, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has also received evidence that VRS forces in the ARK had large amounts of tanks, rockets, other types of weaponry at that time; you're certainly aware of that, right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, I knew that they had weapons that were not there momentarily, but when Yugoslavia disintegrated lots of these weapons from Croatia and Slovenia were brought to our area, to Sarajevo, to all parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Brought there -- many were brought from Croatia to the area of the ARK by the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those weapons were inherited by the VRS when it was created in May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your position at the time was that this gave the VRS a massive military advantage; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And since you mentioned tanks, I'm going to look at just one example of something you said during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 02366. This is going to be a transcript of the 24th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly. I'm going to ask for page 77 in the English and 53 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a portion of a speech that you gave at the Assembly, and in the bottom paragraph on our screens in both languages, you say: "Now we go back to this. We had aviation, howitzers, tanks, cannons, but what did Muslims have? Some gun, some machine-gun that they bought from the Serbs, and homemade guns." This is an example of you expressing the position we discussed a moment ago, that, at the beginning of the war, the VRS had a massive military advantage; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe this Assembly session has already been marked for identification as P6921 and that number has been reserved for excerpts from it. We'll just make sure this is among those excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second. Mr. Mladic, you're not there to give instructions for the curtains to be pulled up. You're not in the position to give any instructions. If there's any matter you would like to raise, then you can do that through counsel. Switch off your microphone, switch off. Then let's get back to -- yes, this will then be a part of that selection to be made from this Assembly session. That's hereby on the record, also what you read to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn back to your positions now. You mention in paragraph 1 of your statement that you were president of the Assembly of the ZOBK and later --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- of the ARK. In both cases --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In both cases, your vice-president of the Assembly was the same man; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: It was Brdjanin, Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The ARK Assembly also had an Executive Council beginning early in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And who was the president of the Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Nikola Erceg. First it was Andjelko Grahovac, and then he was replaced. And then Nikola Erceg came to that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You don't mention your position in your statement, but you were a member of the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the president of that Crisis Staff was Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As president, he would preside over all the meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He would propose the topics to be discussed?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When a meeting was going to be held, you would be notified by phone; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, it depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 31770, page 23 in the English, 33 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up, this will be a portion of your OTP interview. We see at the bottom of the page -- we had previously seen at the bottom of the page in the English but we now no longer have the right pages. Can we have 23 in the English, 33 in the B/C/S. At the bottom of the page in the English and the top of the page in the B/C/S, you're being asked first: "Isn't it correct that even though you did not attend some meetings, but you were present in most of those meetings, ARK Crisis Staff and War Presidency meetings?" And you respond: "It's possible." You were asked: "How would you receive information about a meeting that is going to be held, the ARK Crisis Staff meeting?" And you say: "On the phone, by the phone." And you're asked: "And you, who'd call you on the phone to inform about the meeting?" And you answer -- and I think we turn to the next page in the English here: "I think again it would be Radic, Radic's -- or it was Radic's secretary." Did that refresh your recollection as to how you would be notified about Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Well, I've already said, there were different ways: By telephone, during meetings. The important thing was that I was informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just for the clarity of the record, Radic's secretary who sometimes informed you, that was Predrag Radic's secretary; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: He was the president of Banja Luka municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Someone from the 1st Krajina Corps, either General Talic or someone deputised to attend in his place, would always attend ARK Crisis Staff meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: If the general himself was not there, his deputy would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in 1992, you often saw General Talic visiting the municipal building in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I saw him only once at a Crisis Staff meeting. He may have been there several times, but I didn't see him. And, yes, I did see him in the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You often saw him in the municipality building, setting aside the reasons he was there; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I believe that he visited the president of the municipality and perhaps somebody else as well, maybe the president of the Executive Board who was in charge of the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Setting aside who he was visiting, so I'm not asking you about that at the moment, he was often in the municipal building; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Stojan Zupljanin, the head of the CSB, also was often in the municipal building; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I saw him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And either he or someone else from the police would attend every Crisis Staff meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I did not see Stojan Zupljanin ever at the Crisis Staff meeting, at least at those meetings that I attended. I saw Djuro Golic, his deputy. I didn't see Stojan Zupljanin at a Crisis Staff meeting ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You would often see him together with the Crisis Staff president, Mr. Brdjanin; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I can't say that I saw him often. I didn't even see the president of the Crisis Staff often. I suppose that they did communicate, but I didn't see them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, in the same document, 65 ter 31770, if we could have page 28 in the English and 40 in the B/C/S. So at the top of the page, line 5 in the B/C/S, you can see you're being asked: "Did you see Radoslav Brdjanin and Stojan Zupljanin coming together in the municipal building?" And you answered: "I didn't see them in -- in the building, municipal building, but I would see them in the hotel. I would often see them in hotels." That's the truth, what you said in 2001, that you often saw Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Stojan Zupljanin together; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the moment I'm not asking whether it's possible. What you said in 2001 on this subject, that was the truth, you often saw them together in 1991 and 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I suppose that that was the case. I can't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, under the circumstances, I'd tender this page of the witness's interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit Number P6994, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, have you uploaded the separate page because we have now -- of course, now it's the whole of the document which is in evidence because this is how you uploaded it, and we are talking about 77 pages, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not seeking to tender the entire interview, Mr. President. At the same time, I'd suggest it would be most efficient, as this may recur, to upload a version only after the completion of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. And we'll then instruct Madam Registrar to replace the 77-page document by the one page then uploaded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart now to play a clip from Exhibit P4338.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, this will be a portion of a rally held in Banja Luka in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm told for the booths that I should mention this is the third clip in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And has it -- has the text been verified already or should we play it twice, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm in your hands. I'm reminded that it is an admitted exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's an admitted exhibit. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm told we're having a technical problem, and so I'll move on to my next topic and we'll simply come back to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, I'm going to turn then to the topic of regionalisation. Now, there were two regional bodies in the -- established in the Bosnian Krajina, first the ZOBK and then the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, it was one body but it changed its name. First it was the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, and then it changed its name to the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina, but it was one and the same body.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were describing that transition in your OTP interview, and you said: "All of a sudden it happened that it was allowed to establish such a region." That happened in September 1991, that it was suddenly allowed to establish an autonomous region; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not in September, but in April, on the 24th of April, that's when the region was established. This is the truth. I don't know about September.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, I'm distinguishing now, and I think the date you're referring to is the date of the creation of the ZOBK, the community; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The region, on the other hand, the ARK, that was established in September; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you said in your interview: "All of a sudden it was allowed to establish such a region ..." It also became allowed in September of 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: It was prescribed by the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina provided for the right to establish a region, and then when we were going to do it, that was up to us. It had nothing to do with either the month of April or the month of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, speaking specifically of the ARK, I'd like to look at 65 ter 10741. Now, this is a document coming from the Sarajevo city board of the SDS, and looking just below point 1, we read: "By this we appoint the Staff for observation of implementation of the Decision ..." And in the first point: "On promulgation of autonomous regions as unquestionable parts of the federal state of Yugoslavia and as constituent parts of the federal unit of Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." So the SDS board in Sarajevo is referring to a specific decision taken to promulgate autonomous regions; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not the regions, but the SAO. The only region where I was present was the ARK, and the rest were Serbian autonomous provinces or -- yes, the Serbian autonomous provinces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this refers to, in point 2, a decision and conclusions adopted at the Pale symposium of municipal, regional, and republic SDS organs of 7 September 1991. As a member of the Main Board, you would have attended that symposium; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: From the moment it was established, the Serbian Democratic Party had two Main Boards. I did not attend the first board -- or, rather, I was not its member. It was only the second board that I was a member of. I don't know when that happened and -- well, there is a possibility that I was a member thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you'd give me just a moment. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you say in paragraph 1 of your statement that you were a member of the SDS Main Board, do you recall the dates today on which you were a member?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was perhaps a year later that I became a member of the Main Board. The first Main Board may have been in place for a year, and then a year after that a new Main Board was established and I may have been a member of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the new Main Board -- in fact, that would have been established at the anniversary session of the SDS in July of 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Quite possible at the Assembly, because the Assembly established it. I believe that that was on the 12th of July in -- at the Holiday Inn hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So then you were a member of the Main Board by the time -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness add what year he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That could have been in 1991. But I was a member of the Assembly, not of the Main Board. And maybe at that Assembly meeting, I was also selected as a member of the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As of the date we see here, September 1991, you were in fact a member of the SDS Main Board, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know when the second Main Board was established, if it was then. And if it says that I was there, then I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall attending this Pale symposium of SDS organs on the 7th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi -- let me just have a look. The correction of the year in paragraph 1 was from 1992 to 199 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 90. Now, we are talking about the 12th of July -- let me just have a look. I asked you what year. You said it was 1991, not 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first Main Board was set up in 1990, and then a reformed Main Board was established in 1991. Some people left, some people were recruited into that new Main Board, and all of that happened on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, one question: Was the new board -- is it just that there were new members, that it still was the Main Board of the SDS but different people in that Main Board, or was it a different institution, different body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the same body. Some people left, some people joined, that was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I do, Your Honour, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10741 receives Exhibit Number P6995, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6995 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And mindful of the date of the symposium we just looked at, the 7th of September, I'd ask that we call up 65 ter 20232.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, another member of the SDS Main Board at the time was Jovan Tintor; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: "Da."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a conversation between him and someone named Mirko Jovic. Toward the bottom of page in both languages, Mr. Tintor says: "You know what? We have no, we have no specifics. There will be changes tomorrow ... we passed ... we passed a decision yesterday that Bosnia can remain ... err ... officially ... but we'll split it into Serbian Bosnia, Croatian Bosnia, Muslim Bosnia. Everyone should have their own and ... that'll explode like a bomb tomorrow." He's describing the decision reached on the 7th of September, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the question. I just want to know if there is more documents that would be used and that are not on the list? This document is not on the list. There is many documents, but not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll double-check that, and I'm happy to confer with Mr. Lukic at the break with my outline and the list, but I don't have the list in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if any problem remains, Mr. Lukic, we'll hear after the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I apologise to Mr. Lukic obviously for the omission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when Mr. Tintor refers to a decision that will explode like a bomb, he's referring to the decision on the 7th of September, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I know Jovan Tintor, but I also know Mirko Jovic. Mirko Jovic did not live in Republika Srpska. He lived in the Republic of Serbia in Stara Pazova --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please answer the question, whether, as far as you're aware of, Mr. Tintor refers to the decision mentioned by Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would object. Because how would he know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if he doesn't know, he'll tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah, asking him to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I really don't. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's the same question you didn't object to in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now he was asked whether he knows what other men meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's not -- let's not split hairs over that at this moment. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would object to have this document in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the basis for your objection, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not -- there was no connection established and he knows nothing about this conversation, or he maybe knows but it is not established. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, I think, common practice in this courtroom that evidence closely linked to events described by a witness, even if a witness is not aware of that, can be tendered and will be admitted in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if there is any issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I don't have that document in front of me since it's something new. It's not on the list and it's not given to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to postpone my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different objection. Then you should say: Could I have my time to respond because I don't have it at this moment. That's different from the objection you raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this is granted. We'll mark it for identification, and we'll hear from you -- we'll hear from you once you have had the time to have a closer look at it. Madam Registrar, the document would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 20232 receives MFI P6996, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- and can we have 65 ter 08469.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be the 12 July 1991 session of the SDS that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 126 in the English and 115 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here that 45 members have been elected to the Main Board at this session. If I direct your attention to the name at number 12, does that refresh your recollection as to whether it was in fact July 1991 when you yourself were elected to the SDS Main Board?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the gentleman at number 8, we see Mr. Tintor was also elected at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that I was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's a long document. I just ask that it be marked for identification at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you would then make a further selection later?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 08469 receives MFI P6997, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 06875, and I can tell Mr. Lukic that this one isn't on my list because it's on his. And this should be the statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. If we could have page 2 in both languages at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see here at the top that nine days after that symposium at Pale was when the Autonomous Region of Krajina was established, right, the 16th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't think that it had anything to do with the establishment of the autonomous region; I mean that meeting at Pale. We established the autonomous region even before the political position was voiced. I don't know what happened next, I wasn't there, I don't remember. And the instructions that you have referred to and that you relate to September, I don't know anything about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, witness, witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it wasn't the SDS who told us to set up the autonomous region --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let me stop you there. The simple question was whether this was the 16th of September, and Mr. Traldi says that that's nine days after the symposium. You know, new year six days after at least our Christmas, that doesn't mean that new year is caused by Christmas. There was no question about a causal relationship; it was just establishing a frame. And whatever Mr. Traldi wants to conclude from that -- he didn't ask you -- and we understand it to be just those dates. Please proceed. And, Mr. Traldi, you are aware that if you wanted to suggest something, then of course it should be made explicit and then we would -- it sounds a bit like argument, it must be a relation, although it was not part of your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this be admitted as an associated exhibit. It should get a D number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well -- yes, it was on the list of associated exhibits; therefore, we do not wait further. The D number for this document, Madam Registrar, would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D856, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D856 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution have 65 ter 03173.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here -- and there are a number of articles on the B/C/S page. Do you see the boxed article regarding the declaration of an autonomous region? I see you've nodded, but can you confirm orally that you've seen it?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is from Javnost and it's dated 14 September 1991. And the article explains that on the 12th of September, 1991, the community of municipalities of eastern and old Herzegovina decided to proclaim the Serbian Autonomous District of Herzegovina which would be an integral part of the federal state of Yugoslavia and the federal unit of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is also just a few days after the 7 September conference; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'm putting to you that it is not a coincidence that the 25 September decision from the Sarajevo board refers to a 7 September decision, a 7 September symposium, it says a decision was taken to establish autonomous regions, five days later SAO Herzegovina declared, nine days later the ARK declared. I'm putting to you that that's not a coincidence; that's because these regions were set up at central direction. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: My region where I was president has nothing to do with this date or the Serb party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do we understand the answer to be that -- that you consider it to be a coincidence that these regions were set up and that you are not aware or even deny that they were set up at a central direction. Is that -- you deny that, is that -- or are you not aware of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know about myself and my region. It has nothing to do with the centre and I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a clear answer. Then Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03173 receives Exhibit Number P6998, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 20559; this is another associated exhibit. And this will be an intercepted conversation between Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Stevandic dated the 11th of January, 1992. Turning to page 6 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, President Karadzic, asks Mr. Stevandic: "Well, who invented the regionalisation, was it them or did I invent it?" And Stevandic explains what the leaders in the ARK want, and Karadzic responds: "Listen Nenad, well they cannot... well, we have all of that in the plans, we have all moves in the envelopes, they must not do it before we do it in the whole of Bosnia. Why are they playing smart? They are explaining my policy to me..." And if we turn now to page 11, page 7 in the B/C/S, Stevandic says: "Let me tell you we can't make a round of three houses if we don't support the Krajina option." And Karadzic says: "What do you mean by the Krajina option?" Stevandic says: "The option of that regionalisation and that matter." And President Karadzic says: "The regionalisation has been carried out. What else needs to be done?" Stevandic responds: "Well, Krajina institutions, specifically the government ..." And President Karadzic says: "Well, it will be ... well, why are they being smartasses?! That was my idea, not theirs! ..." What President Karadzic is expressing in this conversation is that regionalisation was his policy; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't think it was his policy. You see that he was late with these proposals and ideas. We were ahead of him. And it's not correct that it's his idea. The entire Krajina was in favour of regions. President Karadzic was not the SDS on his own. The party had its organs, made these decisions and all that. But we, before the SDS, all of us, even other parties too, and all parties in the Krajina, we were in favour of regions in the Krajina, at least at first. He didn't like that. That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The reason you and Mr. Karadzic were moving at different speeds was that, as you've just testified, was that he had a specific plan for when different steps should be implemented; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know what was in his head. We thought of what was our own interest and what would be of benefit to us, and he probably thought that he should have a say in everything and that he should say whatever was supposed to be done. We were so interested in that because we were so backward economically. And also, these relations between and amongst us were not all that great. Well, you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- our thinking went along different lines --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you've gone somewhat beyond the question I asked you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I move on, I'd ask that this be given a D number as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put first one question to the witness. In your statement, paragraph 27, you talk about this conversation, this intercept, and there you say: "Dr. Karadzic popularised the power of Sarajevo, both in terms of the party and the Sarajevo government in general." Can you explain what you mean by that, that he "popularised the power of Sarajevo"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what does it mean? He said one thing and did something else. What we considered to be our political position, that we would have practical advantages from, he sidestepped that and he kept saying that we were right and that there would be a position when we could realise all our positions and we were impatient and we simply did not take into account Radovan Karadzic. At least it seemed to us that Radovan was doing what Alija was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But again, what do you mean by the term "popularised the power of Sarajevo"? What does that mean? Just explain, please, the term you used in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I meant political concentration and concentration of capital in Sarajevo, as was the case. We created a region so that this capital, which enormously prevailed in Sarajevo, turning Sarajevo into a major city, we were looking at lawful ways of returning this to us because we were visibly poorer than Sarajevo. That was a thorn in our side, and when we addressed Radovan on that topic he evaded the issue and avoided us as far as the community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina is concerned. You see here how he is imposing this on Stevandic, that he is right, and he wasn't right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Shall I take it that he was in favour of keeping together Bosnia and Herzegovina with the capital of Sarajevo as the seat of the government? Or what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, that's the way he behaved, let me tell you. There was an attempt to unite the two Krajinas, the one in Croatia and the one that we have here in Bosnia, and that project of unification is something that he stopped. So Radovan Karadzic all the time fought for an Avnoj Bosnia-Herzegovina, for the preservation of an Avnoj Bosnia-Herzegovina. And he kept insisting on that all the time, it prevailed all the time. People from the Krajina, from the Serb Krajina, there was this declaration that the Republic of Serb Krajina would be annexed to the rest of Yugoslavia. So our objective was that that part of the Serb people that was in Croatia and that had lived through terrible things and a terrible crime was committed against them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- during the Second World War, we wanted to annex them to us, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You went far beyond my question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me also see whether I now fully understand. Do I understand that you intended to say that Dr. Karadzic claimed that the power should be in Sarajevo, both party power and government power, and not in the regions and that he imposed more or less his will on the regions, at least he tried to do so? Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Obviously the headquarters of the party was in Sarajevo. He never intended to move the party or any organisation that had to do with the Serb people to Banja Luka. He was firmly attached to Sarajevo and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what I suggested. What I suggested as my understanding of what your testimony now is, is that he claimed that the power should be at the central level rather than in the region, both in terms of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether there's any translation issue there, but "popularised" seems not to be a word that expresses what we now all understand to be the testimony of the witness. Mr. Lukic -- but the witness has explained it now, but if there's any translation issue, then it should be sorted out. It's time for a break, Mr. Traldi. But you first, I take it, wanted to have a decision on tendering this document. Madam Registrar, it is ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 20559 receives Exhibit Number D857, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D857 is admitted. Mr. Kupresanin, we'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, while we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, perhaps you could already inform the Registry which would be the next document you would like to have a look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. 11778, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want it immediately on the screen or just --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to be on notice? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And -- I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is an interview with President Karadzic published in Srpsko Oslobodjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 3 in the English, page 2 in the B/C/S, top of the first column.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: President Karadzic is being asked about the SDS's role in the political struggle through the pre-war Parliament of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. And in the middle of his answer, he says the following: "It was a very successful period of political struggle and the Serbian Democratic Party and its representatives" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking. Mr. Stojanovic, if you keep your earphones on, if Mr. Mladic wants to consult, he has to speak loudly. So would you please then come closer to Mr. Mladic, take off your earphones, so that he can whisper rather than speak aloud. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. But by the time, Your Honour, I take off my headphones ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think my guidance was clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, directing your attention to a portion of President Karadzic's answer here, he says: "It was a very successful period of political struggle and the Serbian Democratic Party and its representatives to the former Assembly came through as the moral winners. We had a list of the actions and steps to take, but we always waited for the Muslims to make a mistake, and after they made one, we created a union of municipalities and the Serbian autonomous areas next, followed by the regions and eventually our Assembly and finally republic." What Karadzic is saying here is, again, that the establishment of autonomous regions was his policy; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was his policy. He's talking about good relations, co-operation, policy, successful policy. He had the law, he had the state, he had the constitution, and what was offered to us on the basis of the constitution is something that we tried to use, and there's no special diplomacy, no special thing about any of this. I don't know how come this text came about. No one prevented us from having regions in Bosnia. Why --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- blowing it out of proportion? Why making such an effort to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, I think you've gone well beyond the question I asked you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd simply tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was your question actually answered?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, and -- so I'll repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Traldi, what you are asking is the witness to interpret the words. What apparently you intend to do is to put to the witness that, contrary to what he said, Mr. Karadzic here apparently is giving a different view on the matters and whether he has any comment on that. That is apparently what you are seeking to do, and the question may easily lead to the kind of answers which are not answers to your question. I leave it to you whether you still want to pursue the matter or whether you would just want the document to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take the point, Mr. President, and I think the most efficient way is simply to tender the document. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We -- Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 11778 receives Exhibit Number P6999, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6999 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask that 65 ter 05995 be brought to the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it comes up, you testified today that you agreed with Mr. Lukic that the objective behind the establishment of regions and the ZOBK specifically was to be the root of a strong Bosnia. In 1992 you believed that the task of the ARK was to "destroy Alija's state"; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: When did I say that in 1992? I don't remember that. I don't remember that I said that Alija's state should be destroyed and that the region is a strong Bosnia. I said that the region was the result of the constitutional law, and I don't know when it was that I said that Bosnia should be destroyed. Do help me, show me some documents, something. These are just assumptions. I mean, I really don't know that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a transcript of the 20th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly in Bijeljina in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 70 in the English and 76 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here we see you speaking. At the beginning of your remarks, you say: "Mr. President, Honourable Assemblymen. "Last year we built up the region and made it strong with a clear purpose and goal. The task of the region of Krajina was to destroy Alija's state." First, can I take it this refreshes your recollection as to whether you said that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Possibly. It's possible I said it. I don't know. When I say "Alija's state," I don't know to what extent it was Alija's state. It was mine as much as it was Alija's, except that Alija was president of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As the second-ranking one, he got --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- 800 something thousand votes at the presidential election and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were only asked if it refreshes your recollection and it apparently does. You said possibly you said this. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you mention the region of Krajina that had this task, you're obviously referring to the ARK, right, yes or no?
