utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you mention Alija's state, you are referring to an independent and unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: When I'm speaking about Alija's state, I'm talking about the Islamic state, based on the Islamic Declaration that was created by Alija Izetbegovic. When I speak about Alija's state, I'm referring to an Islamic state and the Islamic Declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say next: "I think that other regions followed suit and we were successful in that respect." When you say "other regions," you're referring to the SAOs; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning back to the bottom of page 68 in the English and page 75 in the B/C/S, we see a gentleman named Jovo Mijatovic is speaking. Four lines into his remarks, he says something very similar: "At a time when we had to destroy a unitary Bosnia, the SAO regions and districts were politically and territorially the best solution because with them we could round off our territories locally." Mr. Mijatovic is expressing the view that the SAOs were part of destroying the unitary BiH; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this Assembly session be marked for identification. I'll speak with Mr. Lukic about selections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask one question. Sir, is this position described by Mr. Mijatovic the same as the position you described a little earlier when you talked of destroying Alija's state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when I speak about Alija's state, I'm speaking about a unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, excuse me. Just a second. Is he expressing the same sentiment as you or not? Just answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, possibly the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 05995 receives P7000, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7000 is marked for identification, and we are waiting for a selection from the Prosecution. I have one additional question. You said when you were talking about Alija's state, you said it was the Islamic state based on the Islamic Declaration. Now, were you destroying a concept or were you destroying what you considered to have become reality at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reality, and we wanted to break up that concept of an Islamic state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you considered it to have become a reality by then. The speech was delivered in September 1992. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn back now to 1991, and I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a video which has been assigned 65 ter 22372b. I can say ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. I can say it's been confirmed by CLSS and only has to be played once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so therefore the interpretation can be on the basis of the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I receive no translation at all. Is there any sound? Is there any audio available to the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Newscaster: Bosnia and Herzegovina, the so-called plebiscite of the Serb people, has begun earlier today. "Reporter Smiljko Sagolj: Despite decisions of both the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Presidency of this republic proclaiming the plebiscite of the Serb people unconstitutional and illegal, it is nevertheless taking place. "It did not come unexpectedly because the SDS President, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, was explicit. "Radovan Karadzic: We no longer have any obligations towards the BiH Constitution. We have obligations towards the Constitution of Yugoslavia, which guarantees both our right to self-determination and the right of the people to self-organise. "Reporter: When asked if that wouldn't be an act of unconstitutional destruction of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Karadzic replied without a trace of diplomacy, quite unusual for a politician: "Radovan Karadzic: You cannot fuck up the entire Yugoslavia expecting Bosnia to remain a virgin. No way! "Reporter: Let us stress in conclusion that 3 million ballot papers have gone out to polling stations, 2 million for the Serbs, the rest for others. Voting is reportedly also taking place in Serbia, in the US, and everywhere where Serbs live."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The plebiscite that you mention in your statement was also a step towards destroying a unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't think that it was a step to break up Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was the democratic will of the people to express their political views by way of a referendum. Bosnia-Herzegovina had its referendum - I'm referring to the BH Federation, Muslims and Croats - to the extent to which they had this right, we had that right too. We were all constituent peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and this is a democratic right enshrined in international law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 22372b receives Exhibit Number P7001, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7001 is admitted. I see that the CD has been handed over to Madam Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 02335. This is the 3rd Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly held in December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while it comes up, it was your position that the plebiscite showed what territory belonged to the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I did not have a position with regard to those territories, as far as I believe -- I did not even know about some of the territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina where the Serbian population resided.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 26 in the English, 41 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're speaking and you say: "Gentlemen, I want to say that we have formed regions which do not have final borders, i.e., just contours, and in order to achieve that I absolutely agree that we should proceed with separating Serb territories, i.e., Serb municipalities in places where that is possible, specifically on the peripheral areas of our region. "In Bosanska Krajina we have the following situation: We have vast territories, specifically in Prijedor where over 70 per cent, even up to 80 per cent, is Serb territory. The plebiscite has shown us accurately which territory is ours, and in accordance with the plebiscite we have to annex this territory." It was, in fact, your position in 1991 that the plebiscite showed what territory belonged to the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not only the Serbs, all the peoples had the right to join other municipalities, or rather, villages had the right to join various municipalities, municipalities could disappear. It was all the people's democratic right --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- they could use the plebiscite to decide who to live with, so territories could be either joined together or separated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're now giving a long answer explaining your position; however, the same question was put to you before and then you said: "I did not have a position with regard to those territories, as far as I believe." It is now put to you that you said that the plebiscite had determined what was Serb territories, and nothing else was asked. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You continue and say: "I personally think that our living space and the territory in which we live and work is endangered and we have to avert that danger. Actually, we have to prevent Muslims from moving into our territories and regions." That was also your position as of December 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not correct. I never said that. I don't know where this text comes from in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a transcript of the 3rd Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly, sir. I take it in the context of a political debate at that Assembly, you would have been particularly careful to accurately set out our position on what should be Serb territory; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I never said that people should be prevented from moving into any area. It was everybody's democratic right and it is in compliance with the Geneva Conventions on human rights, which says that everybody has the right to free movement. How can you prevent people from doing that? This has been taken out of some context. I don't know where this is from. I don't think I ever, ever said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You then say: "In Cazinska Krajina there are between 250.000 and 300.000 Muslims in a very small space. We can simply shut them off in that ring and it does not suit us at all for them to join us. It is even suitable for us that they are a separate Krajina, the Cazinska Krajina, which will absolutely depend on us in economic terms." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I remember that I tried to communicate with Fikret Abdic about our integration, both physical and economic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I asked you a very simple question. Do you recall saying what the transcript of the 3rd Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly clearly reflects you saying?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask one brief question. You earlier - at least that's how it appears on the transcript - refer to the Geneva Conventions on human rights. Can you explain what exactly you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are basic human rights: The right to property, the right to free movement, the right to life, the right to work. A series of rights that are guaranteed by the international law and various conventions. And one of the rights which is referred to in here is the right to free movement, and the question about that right is whether it was threatened or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties in understanding that that is to be found in the Geneva Conventions, but unless you want to further explain to me, I leave it to that. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In paragraph 16 of your statement, you say that municipalities with a non-Serbian population could join the ARK. So I'd put to you that what you told the Republika Srpska Assembly in December 1991, that it was suitable for the Muslim area to be separate and absolutely dependent, that that's the truth and that your position in your statement is not the truth. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: You're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this Assembly session be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 02335 receives number P7002, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7002 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter 02337. This will be the 4th Session of the Assembly. And if we could have page 37 in the English and 78 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here President Karadzic is speaking. Turning to page 38 in the English and the B/C/S page 79 towards the bottom, we see him say: "We have the right and the ability to prevent anybody on the territories where we conducted our referendum to secede from Yugoslavia. In all territories where Serbs took part in the referendum, regardless whether they make 5 per cent or 55 per cent of the population, they are the constituent element of that town or that republic. All territories where we voted in our referendum to remain within Yugoslavia must stay within Yugoslavia if we decide so." He's saying essentially what you did, that the plebiscite defined Serb territories; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: The plebiscite defined the right to stay in Yugoslavia. We were in Yugoslavia and we wanted to stay in Yugoslavia. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the territories where the outcome said that, you and Mr. Karadzic were saying those had to be Serb territories; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Muslim and Croatian territories could be incorporated as well. It depended on who attended the plebiscite. If a nation decided democratically to stay where they were, why prevent them from doing that? We were in Yugoslavia. We wanted to stay in Yugoslavia. We were in Bosnia, we wanted to stay in Bosnia, on a condition that Bosnia stayed in Yugoslavia. That's what we told people. That's how we organised the plebiscite. The constitution in Yugoslavia and Bosnia and Herzegovina perfectly allowed us to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at the same Assembly session, speakers, including President Karadzic, made clear that if independence was declared, the results would be disastrous, massive bloodshed, hundreds of thousands of people dead; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know where he said that, where he said that there would be hundreds of thousands of people dead and there would be disastrous consequences. On the 14th of October --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- they proclaimed a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the 14th of October. I'm asking about this Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 40 in the English and the bottom of page 83 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while it comes up, you attended this assembly session; right? Sir, I'm not sure if you heard the question at the end. But can you confirm you attended the 4th Session of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Could you please read again what you have just read about the casualties and disastrous consequences? Can I hear that again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll come to that in a minute. The first question is now whether you attended that 4th Session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember whether I attended it or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a moment, sir. But, first, this is another part of President Karadzic's remarks, and he says: "As rational beings we know what civil war means. The experience of Croatia tells us exactly what civil war has done to us. Apart from causing the deaths of several hundred thousand people and complete destruction of several hundred towns, a civil war in Bosnia and Herzegovina would also result in massive and rapid population movements; in other words, it would lead to population homogenisation." So, first, he's clearly saying here that a civil war would result in the deaths of several hundred thousand people, massive destruction, massive population movement; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: It is possible that he said that; however, I did not hear him say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we go back now to page 28 in the English, page 57 in the B/C/S. And here I can tell you the chairman is speaking. And, among other things, we see that he calls for a vote on certain proposals. First, a proposal to emphasise to the president of the United Nations, the embassies in Belgrade, and the member states of the European community that Serbs make up the majority of the population on 65 per cent of the territory of BiH which is unanimously approved. This was the proportion of Bosnia's territory that the Bosnian Serbs claimed as theirs; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Remind me, at what Assembly session was that? Where is this document from? What is its origin?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is the transcript of the 4th Session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to inquire into where the document comes from. We leave that to the parties. If there's anything -- if you have -- you were asked whether you have any recollection. And if you're asking for the date, Mr. Traldi will tell you. But where the document comes from is not something you have to worry about. If there's any worries about that, the parties will raise it, unless you have good reasons to claim that it's a forgery or anything else. Please proceed. And if there's anything to your knowledge in that respect, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. First, do you remember - setting the document aside - that 65 per cent of the territory of Bosnia was roughly what the Bosnian Serbs claimed, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Serbia had about 68 per cent of the territory. Now, whether they had the right to claim that is a different question. They had 62, actually, 62 per cent of the territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991 and 1992. It's official data.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, below this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the witness did not really answer your question. The question was whether the Serbs claimed that territory, not whether they had a right to claim that. As you said, you are uncertain about that. Let's leave apart whether they had a right to do that. The question was whether they claimed that territory. Did they or did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was their probably and everything's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By saying "it was their property," do you mean to say that they claimed that their property was theirs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was private property, and private property is guaranteed. My land, my house, and I had a title of deed before the war and thereafter. I had the right to that property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Witness, this discussion is not about whether I own a piece of land. I think this whole discussion is about who will rule that region or that municipality, so you're now twisting to a different subject. Because the claim is not a claim of property but the claim is a claim of sovereignty or whatever, but rule over those areas. And you are moving away from what clearly is the issue raised by Mr. Traldi. Did the Serbs claim 65 per cent of the territories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where they claimed right, in what territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that, again, was not the question but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below that, we see the decision to establish the Republic of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was unanimously adopted. And then I think we'd turn to the next page in the B/C/S, or at least scroll to the bottom. We see point 2: "Recognition of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." And you are called upon to read out that proposed decision. Now, does that refresh your recollection as to whether you attended this session?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I never attended a session where the Republic of Serbian Krajina would be proclaimed. Not that I don't remember. I was never there --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not proclaimed, recognised by the Serb Assembly in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's a decision you read out and turning to the -- or scrolling down the page, we can see --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't do that. I didn't read out anything. I did not attend that Assembly session. I'm sure that I would remember if I had been. It was a historical moment for the Serbs in Croatia. I'm sure I would remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, I think you might be misunderstanding my question. I'm not asking about an assembly session where the Republic of Serbian Krajina was declared; I'm asking about a session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held December 21st, 1991, at which that Assembly, after declaring the Republic of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, then recognised the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends. Would you be careful. Do we have to ask the witness to take his earphones --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The problem I see is we constantly have wrong B/C/S page. So something's -- this is the third time we have wrong B/C/S page in front of the witness; one of them is this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then get the right page before us. Mr. Traldi, any suggestion as --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It looks like at the bottom of this page we see the decision to form the Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is the one that immediately precedes the one he's called upon to read out. So let's take the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In B/C/S, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In B/C/S, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is the right page. Mr. Lukic, it seems that number 2 appears at two-thirds of the page, and I see that Mr. Kupresanin is referred to there, first apparently invited and then appears as a speaker. Perhaps we could move to the next page then in English as well so that we know what Mr. Kupresanin is recorded as having read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is why I asked for the correct page. On the page 67, line 20 and further, the question was about Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was declared. That's completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No. At page 67, line 20 and further, I said the question was not about Republic of Serbian Krajina being declared. The question was about him attending a session where the Bosnian Serb Assembly recognised it, and we can see him reading out that decision on this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's first -- you are alerted, Mr. Traldi, that Mr. Lukic is -- has some concerns about whether you accurately reflect what is recorded here. I'll take it that you'll keep that in mind. Mr. Lukic, if there's any further problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I confirmed with my friend, my colleague Stojanovic, but I think it was translated as meaning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It could be that there is a translation issue. If that's the case, of course Mr. Traldi will accept that, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's now move to where Mr. Kupresanin is recorded as speaking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say: "Serbian ladies and gentlemen, dear guests, let me first of all congratulate you on the establishment of Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and wish you a lot of success and a lot of happiness. "It is my great honour to send this message" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... which I am going to read out in a moment on behalf of the Serbian Assembly" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we'll have to turn to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... and the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina to our Serbian people in the former Croatian republic. It reads as follows: "In accordance with Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Provisional Statute of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina at its Session on 21 December 1991 has adopted a decision on the recognition of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." We see several lines below this that that was unanimously adopted. So does this refresh your recollection as to whether you attended this Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know whether I attended that session. I don't remember that I ever read this out. I don't remember that session at all. I've never seen or heard this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this session also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 02337 receives P7003, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Mr. Traldi, it's not the usual time for a break, but I would prefer to have a little bit earlier break. After the break, we would then have another 45 minutes left. Mr. Kupresanin, you may follow the usher. We would like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we'll resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could for the sake of efficiency pull up 65 ter 20628.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have page 3 in the English, the bottom of page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a transcript of an intercepted conversation between you and President Karadzic on the 24th of February, 1992. You're talking, as you say in your statement, about negotiations in Lisbon. President Karadzic says: "We achieved maximum success because we achieved that Bosnia cannot be a single state anymore and that it will be composed of three republics. In one paper they even called them states." You ask him who would get the police, and he says: "It would be our police." You say: "Our police on our territory." He says: "Our police on our territory. Our national guard on our territory. Our national guard, and we're pushing further: Our army on our territory ..." Turning to page 6, both languages. You say: "If we already have our territory and our police, then virtually nobody can tell us where our borders are on that territory." President Karadzic says: "Nobody can apart from us." You say: "Apart from us, that's right." He says: "Nobody apart from us." And you say: "That means that practically it's a sovereign, independent state." You and President Karadzic at this point were both seeking to effectively create a Bosnian Serb state; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I know about the Lisbon Agreement. It doesn't put it that way, and this conversation I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking you how the Lisbon Agreement puts it, sir. I'm putting to you as of the 24th of February, 1992, you and President Karadzic were both seeking to create a Bosnian Serb state; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I cannot remember this, and I don't know that I talked to Radovan in this way on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, irrespective of this conversation, which Mr. Traldi used as a kind of an introduction, at that point in time were you seeking an independent Bosnian Serb state to be established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, of course, the next question would be whether you have any comment on what is recorded here because it at least suggests that you were speaking words to the contrary of the answer you gave a second ago. Any comments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question. You just said: "This conversation I really cannot remember." Have you ever seen this transcript of the conversation of the intercepted communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the first time I see it, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 -- just a moment. In paragraph 29 of your statement, you refer to this document and you say: "I have been shown this document," with this number, "a telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and me."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How is it possible that you talk about this document in your statement of 20 March 2014, this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I know of the Lisbon Agreement and I know what it offered, and I know that it suited us and that the Muslims were against it. The international community verified that but Alija didn't want to sign it. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, in paragraph 28, you say: "I have been shown document 65 ter 20604, a telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and me. The conversation shows that Brdjanin and Vukic did not think about the parties' views and just implemented their own ideas" -- sorry, I was at the wrong paragraph. Earlier I said it: "I have been shown document 65 ter 26208, a telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and me ..." That was shown to you, according to your own statement, earlier this year. Any comment about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that that was shown to me, that I had seen that. This is the first I hear about this. I only know of the Lisbon Agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you attested to the truthfulness of your statement. Your statement says: I have been shown document so and so. Therefore, if it is true what you said that you don't remember that I -- or that you had not seen that ever before, I would have expected you in court to tell us: Paragraph 29, I don't know whether that's true or not because I have no recollection whatsoever, that this was shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. I mean, I may remember and I may not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine, but you should tell us. You attested to the truthfulness of your statement, including paragraph 29.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're telling us in your statement that the conversation concerns the Cutileiro Plan so apparently you have any recollection about the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that I ever discussed the topic with Radovan. There were conversations between him and me, but the Lisbon Agreement, I don't remember that we talked about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then you should have told us instead of giving a statement like we find it in paragraph 29. That's your evidence. Apparently you remembered in March that your conversation was about the Cutileiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what the Cutileiro Plan is, but this conversation, no. Maybe I did talk about that subject, the Cutileiro Plan; but that I talked about it this way, as presented here, questions like this, I don't remember any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you aware that you are undermining your own testimony at this moment by saying: This is the statement, I attested to it a couple of hours ago, and now you say: Well, of course I don't know what this was all about, whether there was a telephone conversation. Was it shown to you in March of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when, when, when did I say a couple of hours ago that I accepted that? When did I accept that a couple of hours ago? When? When?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked whether this statement you'd given is truthful, and you said it was. Or have you not read the statement prior to coming to this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would rather be that I hadn't remember -- that I hadn't read it. I mean, I don't remember this at all, a talk -- a conversation between Radovan and me about the Cutileiro Plan, I have no idea whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you are testifying about that conversation, which you say was shown to you. So I take it that both the transcript of that conversation was shown to you in March, that you recently reviewed your own statement in which you say that it was shown to you and that you're commenting on the conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, I would remember that, wouldn't I? When did I see this document? I never saw this document. Had I ever seen it, I would have remembered it. I would have remembered the conversation after all. It was a conversation that was very important for our people, but I don't remember this at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please be aware that by saying that it was not shown to you that you are accusing more or less the Defence -- yes, I do understand that in May of this year that you met with Mr. Lukic and that you reviewed your statement with him in May of this year. It was in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In May this year in The Hague? What do you mean in May this year in The Hague? Well, this is the first time that I'm in The Hague since last year, August -- November. I was not in The Hague in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We received a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says date 8th of December, only down there it was left 6, 7th, and 8th May. It should be December. Now I noticed this mistake as well. But date is 8th of December when I sent this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's just -- yes, it's causing quite a bit of confusion. But you are reported as having reviewed your statement over the last week, the 6th, the 7th, and the 8th of December, to have gone through your statement, and you're telling us that the document to which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's possible that -- it's possible that I went through all of those statements without noticing this and I signed it nevertheless. It's possible. I'm not saying it's not possible. I'd like to be able to remember, but I just don't remember. This is an interesting conversation, very interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not seeking your comment on whether the intercept is interesting or not. We'll -- we've heard your answers to my questions. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask one question. Do you have any reason why, when you were asked whether this statement is truthful, you didn't say: No, I can't confirm this because I didn't read everything in it? Why did you say on the contrary, that you confirm it, it's truthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember that. I cannot say something is truthful if I just don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did this morning, Mr. Kupresanin. Let's leave it to that for the time being. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31773, paragraph 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, as it comes up, this will be your signed statement in the Karadzic case, given to the Karadzic Defence. I imagine you recall that you also, during your testimony in the Karadzic case, attested that your Karadzic Defence statement was truthful and accurate. Do you recall attesting to that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I said that it was truthful and accurate, the statement that I gave in relation to the Defence of Radovan Karadzic, it's true. And everything that I have provided is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 31 of that statement which we have in the English and we're still pulling up the B/C/S -- and, I apologise, I didn't have the B/C/S page number at my finger-tips. And I thank the Court Officer. We see here the same language that you'd been shown an intercepted -- or a telephone conversation between Dr. Karadzic and yourself about the Cutileiro Plan. Now, today you said you couldn't remember if you'd ever talked to Dr. Karadzic about the Cutileiro Plan. You've sworn to two Trial Chambers at this Tribunal in the last 13 months and in two signed statements in the same period of time that not only had you spoken to Dr. Karadzic about the Cutileiro Plan but that you'd recently reviewed the conversation in which you did so; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I repeat, I don't remember. You're trying to convince me that I should remember, but I don't need to remember. I stand by what I signed on behalf of Radovan Karadzic. I don't know if this was shown to me in the Karadzic case. Since this is an interesting conversation, I remember it, I will remember it now. I can remember, I cannot remember. Why shouldn't I remember? Why is this a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's an interesting set of questions, sir. Do you remember it now or not?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't. I'm surprised that I signed it in the Karadzic case. I don't remember it. I'm sure I would remember this. I know all the parts of Radovan's defence. It was a long time ago. I remember that, but I don't remember this document. The Lisbon Agreement was in favour of the Serbs. Why would I be against that agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll stop you there. Let's move on, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, normally, as it's an associated exhibit, I would suggest it get a D number. Under the current circumstances, I'm not sure it satisfies the test as an associated exhibit. I would nonetheless tender it. I'm in the Chamber's hands how to address it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assign a P number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20628 receives Exhibit Number P7004, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7004 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could the Prosecution now have 65 ter 02345. This will be a transcript of the 8th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly on the 25th of February, 1992, the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I have on my note here 65 ter 31773. Are you doing anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No. I would -- I will seek to agree with Mr. Lukic that it's the same paragraph that appears in the statement, but I will attempt to do that rather than tendering any portion of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course it is a matter which draws more and more the attention of the Chamber that, from what was just read a second ago, that it's again literally the same language. We have seen this before, and I think it's good that the Defence is aware that the Chamber -- that it's not unnoticed. That statements taken in the Karadzic case often sometimes with small corrections are literally the same as the ones presented in the Mladic case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 60 in the English and 75 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, do you recall attending the 8th Session of the Assembly of the Bosnian Serb People on the 25th of February.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Do I remember? It is possible that I was. It would be logical that I was, but I can't remember this particular session. How shall I remember? There were so many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, do you recall saying to the Assembly, as you say on this page: "Therefore, I am against any kind of joint institution with the Muslims and Croats of BH. I personally consider them to be our natural enemies. You already know what natural enemies are and that we can never again live together. We can never again do anything together." Do you recall saying that to the Bosnian Serb Assembly?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember. I would remember this. These words carry certain weight. As for natural enemies, we all know what natural enemies are. For example, a dog and a cat are natural enemies, and they deal with each other on the basis of instinct. And, as for human beings, we have common sense, we have reason, that's how we function. Natural enemies are dogs and cats. I don't remember that I ever said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd seek to mark for identification this session as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 02345 receives Exhibit P7005, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is marked for identification and a further selection will be given notice of by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it was around this time, sir, in fact, it was in this same Assembly session that you called on President Karadzic to come out to the ARK Assembly and stop the ARK independence movement; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I did invite Radovan Karadzic to the ARK Assembly but not at that Assembly session that you are talking about. I know that I phoned him to invite him because of the situation that prevailed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: -- I mean in the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I wanted him to assist me, to help me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, you needed him to help you because of his power and influence; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Because his intention was for that to happen, and that was not my intention. They didn't intend for that to happen, for a state to be created in the ARK, and some of our opponents in the same political party and in some other political parties wanted to have a state of Krajina created in the territory of Krajina. And since I know that Radovan Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm stopping you again. Why not answer the question? Was it because of the power and the influence that you asked for his help, of course having --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A simple answer to a relatively simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 64 in the English and 82 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we see you speaking again at this session. Turning to page 65 in the English, you say: "I think a Krajina state -- sorry, I said that a Krajina state is not a realistic idea. It is fiction. To establish it would be a crime against and the destruction of the Serbian people." And then you explain that you can't bear the entire burden of the ARK Assembly on your own shoulders. And at the bottom of the page in the English, turning to the top of page 83 in the B/C/S, you say: "I therefore urge that the president of the party and the president of the Assembly come to Banja Luka to the Assembly and I am sure that nothing bad will happen." So you did, aside from your phone conversation, call on President Karadzic to come to Banja Luka to the ARK Assembly at this Assembly session; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: It is true that I invited him to that session. I know that I spoke to him on the phone. I don't know whether I did it verbally, but it doesn't really matter. The most important thing was that he had been invited and that he had arrived and that, as a result of that, what happened, happened. The outcome of that Assembly session was unexpected --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, the most important thing is that you tell us the truth. I read to you one of your previous answers: "I did invite Radovan Karadzic to the ARK Assembly but not at that Assembly session that you are talking about." You are recorded to have invited him at that Assembly session, and you admitted that you may have done so. Therefore, the answer that you did not do that at that Assembly session is just not the truth. You may have forgotten about it, then you could have told us; but a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have forgotten. I don't remember that. I remember the telephone conversation, though --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then remind you that the proper answer would have been: I remember that I invited him by telephone; however, I do not remember whether I also invited him at the session, instead of saying: I did not do it at the session. You should be more accurate and more precise with your answer. Witness -- witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just said that a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier said something different, and I'm not used to be interrupted by a witness. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say after that in this transcript: "I know that Karadzic as the president of the SDS is truly the leading figure among the Serbian people and five of his sentences are enough to change the entire course of the session, but I am now powerless with those people." What you're saying is that Karadzic, because of his power, could prevent the ARK from seceding from the RS, but you yourself could not; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: Not from Republika Srpska, but from Bosnia-Herzegovina. Not from Republika Srpska, no. They wanted the ARK to stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that's why I invited Radovan. Again, we meet the same stumbling block, make a distinction between the regional Krajina and the Krajina within Bosnia-Herzegovina. I invited Radovan to come and to prevent the creation of the state of Krajina within Bosnia-Herzegovina. We are all again speaking at cross-purposes. That's that. What region of Krajina? People wanted a state of Krajina within Bosnia-Herzegovina. They wanted a state within a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, President Karadzic did come to the next session of the ARK Assembly after this; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have 65 ter 06884.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an extract from the minutes of the 14th Session of the ARK Assembly on the 29th of February, 1992. Now, in the days between the 25th and the 29th of February, the constitution had been promulgated; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: What constitution? Whose constitution? Please, whose constitution? The constitution of Republika Srpska, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 2 in the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, your question was about the constitution. The witness asked: What constitution --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think assuming that you intended to refer to the constitution of the Republika Srpska or the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that he answered that question. Was that what you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in the English, which we now have, towards the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S. We see Radovan Karadzic presented the current political and security situation at the Assembly. We see he gives an explanation and he says, among other things: "If BH changes its status in Yugoslavia, we will change our status too. If BH leaves Yugoslavia, we will leave it too, but not as part of their BH but as our BH, a Serbian one ..." And below that, we see that his report on the political and security situation was accepted in full by the ARK Assembly. And below point 2, turning to the next page in the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you quoted previously was also on page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise. And I thank Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the second paragraph below point 2 that we see here, we see that he stresses that: " ... it would be a crime against the Krajina if it were declared a Republic." That he refers to those as "childish ideas," and then we see "conclusions."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We can turn to page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: After a debate, the deputies in the Assembly of the ARK accepted the Constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH in full. The status of the Autonomous Region of Krajina would be incorporated into the Constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People of BH and strict control of the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina would be established. 148 deputies voted for these conclusions - that's at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S - and none voted against. So President Karadzic accepted your invitation. When he came to the ARK, the ARK Assembly unanimously adopted his position and remained part of the Serbian Republic of BH; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I don't know that a state or a republican law was ever adopted at an Assembly session. I don't know that that was foreseen by the constitution. Why would the constitution of Republika Srpska be discussed at the Parliament of the autonomous region if we have the Parliament of Republika Srpska? Only the Assembly of Republika Srpska could adopt such constitution. Everything else is absurd. I'm sure that Radovan did participate in the debate, but not regarding the topic of the state constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it your position that this is not an accurate reflection of what happened at that session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The constitution was not discussed at that session. I know that. We discussed issues and I know what those were. None of them was the constitution. The most important issue was to prevent the setting up of the state of Krajina of north-Western Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was a different one. Does this not reflect the discussion at they took place at the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that this record is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any fact to your knowledge which would support that opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I remember, and I have just shared with you, I don't see a stamp, I don't see my signature, nothing. I would not be in a position to sign a document adopting the republican constitution. It would have been pointless to discuss that at the regional Assembly. The only place, the only proper place where to discuss that and to adopt that would be the republican Assembly or Parliament.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's logic. I'm asking about facts. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, in the interests of time, I see it's almost 2.15, I'm not going to pull up the examples but I'm going to put to you that this is a document that you've also said in two signed statements that you've attested to in the last 13 months that you've been shown this document and that you've made comments on, and on neither of those occasions have you said in your statements which were -- which you attested were truthful, on neither of those occasions have you said: These minutes are not an accurate reflection of what happened at that Assembly. So I'd put to you that what you're saying now is, in fact, not the truth. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN
utterances.text: I can see my name here but there is no signature, there is no stamp. How come that I did not sign this document? Anybody could have been drafted it. Anybody could have submitted it to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, this document was shown to you by the Mladic Defence, by the Karadzic Defence. You were asked to comment on it. You did. You didn't say: It's not what it claims to be. You just gave other comments. You have not told us that this does not reflect what was discussed during that meeting. Why didn't you do that? Why is it that now in court suddenly not in the Karadzic case but in this case you suddenly say: Well, whatever comment I gave, it's not accurately reflecting what had happened and therefore I refrain from commenting on it because it's not a truthful document. Why didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever documents I signed and stamped, I recognise as documents. This, in my view, is not a document. This was just filed with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why didn't you then say that when interviewed by the Defence teams of Mr. Karadzic and of Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no stamp. How can I proffer any comments? I suppose that at that time I failed to not see the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it to that. It is -- the last part of the answer is of some relevance to the question put to the witness. Mr. Traldi, it's time for -- to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before we do and so I don't forget, I'd just tender the document as in a previous similar instance I'd suggest a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Madam Registrar, a P number to be assigned to this document would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7006, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7006 is admitted into evidence -- is marked for identification. I stand corrected. Then we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's a very brief document which I'd ask to have admitted so if in case the Chamber is asking for follow-up from me, I would just inquire as to the reason for marking it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree it's a three-page document only so, therefore, a further selection would not make that much sense. I stand corrected again. P7006 is now finally admitted into evidence. Mr. Kupresanin, we'll adjourn for the day. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.30 -- no, no, we'll continue on Monday, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony or to communicate in any other way with whomever it may be about your testimony, whether that is testimony given today or whether that is testimony still to be given on Monday. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I heard the word "svedok," which means that Mr. Mladic was talking about a witness or this witness or whatever. He should not speak aloud, make that clear to him, because it will have similar consequences as before when he continues to do so. We'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume Monday, the 15th of December, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.
